title: Get all global objects of an expression — findGlobals
text: expr R expression. envir environment search globals. attributes TRUE (default), attributes expr also searched. FALSE, . character vector, attributes matching names searched. Note, attributes attributes' elements searched, , attributes searched recursively.  Also, attributes searched dotdotdot = "ignore". tweak optional function takes expression returns tweaked expression. dotdotdot TBD. method character string specifying type search algorithm use. substitute TRUE, expression substitute():ed, otherwise . unlist TRUE, list unique objects returned. FALSE, list length(expr) sublists. trace TBD. locals globals part "local" environment function included ? mustExist TRUE, error thrown object identified global located.  Otherwise, global returned. recursive TRUE, found globals searched additional globals. example, closure (function) exists outside package namespace may contain additional globals. Similarly, formula may depend globals. skip (internal) list globals searched additional globals.  Ignored unless recursive TRUE. ... used.

title: Get all global objects of an expression — findGlobals
text: findGlobals() returns character vector. globalsOf() returns Globals object.

title: Get all global objects of an expression — findGlobals
text: currently three strategies identifying global objects. method = "ordered" search method identifies globals global variable preceding local variable name dropped (unlike "conservative" method). method = "conservative" search method tries keep number false positives minimum, .e. identified objects likely true global objects.  time, risk true globals identified (see example). search method returns exact result findGlobals() function codetools package. method = "liberal" search method tries keep true-positive ratio high possible, .e. true globals likely among identified ones.  time, risk false positives also identified. method = "dfs" search method identifies globals abstract syntax tree (AST) using depth-first search, better emulates R engine identifies global variables. recursive = TRUE, globals part locally defined functions also found, otherwise .

title: Get all global objects of an expression — findGlobals
code: b <- 2 expr <- substitute({ a <- b; b <- 1 })  ## Will _not_ identify 'b' (because it's also a local) globalsC <- globalsOf(expr, method = "conservative") #> Error: bad assignment: ‘2 <- 1’ print(globalsC) #> Error: object 'globalsC' not found  ## Will identify 'b' globalsL <- globalsOf(expr, method = "liberal") #> Error: bad assignment: ‘2 <- 1’ print(globalsL) #> Error: object 'globalsL' not found

title: Version 0.18.0
text: Add findGlobals(..., method = "dfs"), finds globals R expressions walking abstract syntax tree (AST) using depth-first search. new approach better job emulating R engine identifies global variables. example, new "dfs" method picks x local({ function(x) x; x }) global variable, "ordered" method fails . Analogously, globalsOf() gained support method = "dfs" Now findGlobals() supports expression objects, e.g. findGlobals(expression(x + y)). now possible specify multiple method search algorithms findGlobals() globalsOf(), combine results , e.g. findGlobals(expr, method = c("dfs", "ordered")).
